Question_text: TWH makes a range of toys using batch production. TWH's Managing Director, Dylan, plans to invest in new technology to reduce average costs. 'It's the only way to increase efficiency as I do not know how we can improve employees' motivation' he said. Dylan cannot decide on whether it would be better to use retained profits or a long term loan as the source of finance. Table 1: Data for 2014 includes Number of toys made per week (260000), Number of employees (500), Average wage per hour paid by TWH ($6), and Average wage per hour paid by similar businesses ($6.50).
image: Table 1, titled 'Data for 2014', presents four rows of data. The first row shows 'Number of toys made per week' as 260000. The second row shows 'Number of employees' as 500. The third row shows 'Average wage per hour paid by TWH' as $6. The fourth row shows 'Average wage per hour paid by similar businesses' as $6.50.
Sub_topic: Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production
Factors in choice: size, legal form, amount, time, loans
Classify costs: fixed, variable, average, total
Financial rewards: wage, salary, bonus, commission, profit sharing
Non-financial: job enrichment, rotation, teamworking, training, promotion
Reasons for finance: start-up, expansion, working capital

Parts.part_text: What is meant by ‘average cost'?
Calculate the output per employee per week in 2014.
Identify and explain two possible advantages to TWH of using batch production.
Identify and explain two ways that TWH could improve the motivation of its employees.
TWH can either use retained profit or a long term loan to finance the purchase of new technology. Which option do you recommend TWH should use? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Ramford is a private limited company with four factories making a wide range of food products. The Finance Director is concerned about financial performance and mentions 'diseconomies of scale', leading to a decision to cut product lines from 80 to 10. Table 2: Extract from accounts shows data for 2013 and 2014, including Revenue (sales) ($m), (Net) profit ($m), Capital employed ($m), Net profit margin, and Return on Capital Employed.
image: Table 2, titled 'Extract from accounts', presents financial data for the years 2013 and 2014. For 2013, Revenue (sales) is $200m, (Net) profit is $70m, Capital employed is $280m, Net profit margin is 35%, and Return on Capital Employed is 25%. For 2014, Revenue (sales) is $150m, (Net) profit is $60m, Capital employed is $300m, with Net profit margin and Return on Capital Employed as unknown (marked with '?').
Sub_topic: Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Causes of failure: management skills, environment changes, liquidity
Concept of diseconomies, examples: communication, commitment, coordination
Product life cycle: stages, extension strategies
Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio

Parts.part_text: What is meant by a ‘private limited company'?
Identify two causes of business failure.
Identify and explain two diseconomies of scale that Ramford might be experiencing.
Identify and explain two factors that Ramford should consider when deciding which products to remove from its product range.
Do you think the Finance Director is right to be worried about the financial performance of Ramford in 2014? Justify your answer using the data in Table 2 and appropriate ratios.

Question_text: Grimshaw manufactures mobile (cell) phones for the mass market. Last year its market share increased by 3%. The Managing Director is planning to set up a new factory in country T to supply the mobile phone market in that country for the first time. Grimshaw plans to sell a new model of mobile phone. The Managing Director has asked for market research to be done. He said: 'As a multinational, we can set up a new factory anywhere; I want to know whether the Government of country T will offer us any help to build our factory there.'
Sub_topic: Different objectives: survival, growth, profit, market share
Benefits to country/economy: jobs, exports, choice, investment
Drawbacks to country/economy: local sales reduction, profit repatriation

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'mass market'?
What is meant by 'market share'?
Identify and explain two advantages of market research to Grimshaw.
Identify and explain two advantages to Grimshaw of developing new products.
Do you think the Government of country T should help businesses such as Grimshaw set up in its country? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Tebo has recently been made redundant from his job as a car mechanic. He is thinking of setting up his own business. Even though he has no management experience, he knows that managing cash flow will be important to the success of the business. Tebo is considering whether to apply for a FIXIT franchise. This franchise would cost $15000, which would use all of his savings. FIXIT is a car repair franchise, with 36 franchisees.
Sub_topic: Functions: planning, organising, coordinating, commanding, controlling
What is cash-flow forecast, construction, importance
Overcome short-term problems: overdraft, delay payments, quicker debtor payments
Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Contents of business plan, assistance to entrepreneurs

Parts.part_text: What is meant by ‘made redundant'?
Identify two functions of management that Tebo might have to perform.
Explain why managing cash flow will be important for Tebo's business.
Identify and explain two factors Tebo should consider when deciding where to locate his business.
Do you think that buying a FIXIT franchise is the best way for Tebo to start his business? Justify your answer.
